items.title: Advance voting begins in Toronto, Mississauga
items.summary: Voters can start casting their ballots for the municipal eleciton in Toronto and Mississauga on Tuesday. m. m. Locations where you can vote will be listed on your Voter ID card. When you go to vote, take a piece of identification with you that has your name and Toronto address on it to show the election official. It does not need to be photo ID. You can find more details here. m. m. Any eligible voter can vote at any of the advance voting locations. Both the mayoral races in these cities are expected to come down to the wire. In Mississauga, incumbent Carolyn Parrish is facing off against former mayor Bonnie Crombie and councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla. Meanwhile, incumbent Olivia Chow is facing a challenge from Councillor Brad Bradford and former MP Chris Alexander in Toronto. m.

items.title: Mississauga: 74% Reject Insults After Heated Debate
items.summary: Following the October 1 debate, 74% reject personal insults and just 14% describe the campaign as mostly respectful. The rejection crosses candidate lines. October 6, 2026 (Toronto, ON) - A new Liaison Strategies Mississauga survey finds 74% of residents say personal comments or insults about other candidates are unacceptable during an election campaign. Only 14% describe the mayoral campaign as mostly respectful. The October 2-4 poll was conducted immediately after the October 1 debate, which CityNews reported featured personal exchanges between Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. Liaison surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from October 2 to October 4, 2026, using Interactive Voice Recording (IVR) technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialling (RDD) across both landline and cellular phone networks. The resulting data was weighted to match targets based on the 2021 Census. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20, and is higher for subsamples. Results may not add to 100% due to rounding. Liaison Strategies is one of the most accurate polling firms in Canada. It ranked #1 in accuracy in the 2025 Ontario election and #2 nationally in the 2025 federal election. Liaison is a member of the Canadian Research Insights Council. David Valentin, Principal at Liaison Strategies, said: "The campaign clashes have put campaign conduct in the spotlight.

items.title: Most Mississauga residents don’t want to see personal attacks in the mayoral election — but that doesn’t stop clips going viral
items.summary: Following an “out of control” debate, Mississauga residents claim personal attacks are unacceptable A composite image of four photographs show, from left to right: Bonnie Crombie, Dipika Damerla, Carolyn Parrish and Alvin Tedjo. Most Mississauga residents describe the current mayoral campaign as mostly mean-spirited or a mix of respectful and mean-spirited following a heated debate last week, according to a poll from Liaison Strategies. Three-quarters of residents said personal comments or insults are unacceptable during an election campaign, and just under a third said the race has featured mostly personal attacks. About 30 per cent said there was a mixture of personal and policy, while 17 per cent said it had been mostly fair political debate. ” The poll was conducted in the two days after the debate, which has been shared widely in clips online. “It’s interesting that people are picking up on it,” said Liaison Strategies principal David Valentin. “We know that people aren’t watching debates as much but they are getting clips. They are seeing little snippets. ” But as much as people say they don’t like this kind of behaviour from their elected officials, Valentin said, their actions may indicate otherwise. “Voters routinely tell us that they hate negative campaigning and hate negative ads. And yet nothing is more effective than negative ads,” he said.

items.title: Boy recounts 1994 park attack on tape played at trial of alleged sex predator
items.summary: Thirty-two years after a 10-year-old boy was tied to a tree and sexually assaulted, an audio tape of his September 1994 police interview was played for the jury Monday at the trial of his alleged attacker. Richard Neil has pleaded not guilty to 17 historical charges linked to attacks on three children.

items.title: Land Secured in Lakeview Village for Peel Police's New 600-Officer Division in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Region of Peel has finalized a land deal in Lakeview Village to build a new Peel Regional Police 14 Division in southeast Mississauga. Ward 1 Councillor Stephen Dasko announced the acquisition Monday evening, calling it a significant milestone for public safety in the growing waterfront community. The new division is expected to bring roughly 600 officers and support staff to the area, adding a substantial police presence to Ward 1 and its surroundings. Dasko said he has spent several years working with the region, Peel Regional Police and Lakeview Village representatives to get the project to this stage. The region awarded a contract for architectural consulting services back in April after issuing a request for proposals earlier in the year, and the design is now moving through its conceptual phase. A construction-industry project listing describes the planned complex as a 7,430-square-foot, two-storey police and fire facility paired with a 9,300-square-foot, three-storey parking garage. Insauga reports construction isn't expected to begin before 2028, meaning the new division is still years away from opening its doors.

items.title: Latest polls show tight race for mayor in Mississauga
items.summary: Given results from the latest polls, it appears the hotly contested mayoral race in Mississauga is up for grabs with three weeks remaining until election night. Two of three polls to release results the past couple of days have former mayor Bonnie Crombie with narrow leads over Mayor Carolyn Parrish while a third shows the incumbent with a nine-point advantage over her predecessor. Liaison Strategies said Monday morning its latest Mississauga Tracker survey finds Crombie at 30 per cent, Parrish at 29 per cent, Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo at 26 per cent and Ward 7 Coun. Dipika Damerla at 11 per cent among decided and leaning voters. The remaining four per cent said they’d vote for someone else. ” An August Liaison poll showed Parrish and Crombie tied at 35 per cent, Damerla with 18 per cent and Tedjo with 12 per cent. For its latest poll, Liaison said it surveyed a random sample of 1,000 Mississauga residents from Oct. 2-4 using Interactive Voice Recording technology. Participants were reached through random digit dialing across both landline and cellphone networks. 1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20, and is higher for subsamples, including decided and leaning voters, Liaison noted. David Valentin, principal at Liaison Strategies, observed Crombie has a narrow lead over Parrish, with Tedjo closing the gap.

items.title: Parrish Skips Two Debates Monday as Crombie, Tedjo and Damerla Face Off Twice in One Day
items.summary: According to Insauga, three of Mississauga's four main mayoral candidates faced off twice on Monday while Mayor Carolyn Parrish sat out both events. Bonnie Crombie, Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla squared off Monday morning at the Mississauga Convention Centre in a housing-focused debate co-hosted by the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board and the Cornerstone Association of Realtors. The same three candidates were set to debate again Monday night at Mississauga City Hall, this time hosted by Policorner, an organization that covers politics and related news at Queen's Park. Insauga notes Parrish did not join her rivals at either event, despite telling the outlet back in July that she planned to take part in three debates before the Oct. 26 election. The housing debate asked candidates to lay out their visions for the city and address issues including affordability and housing supply.

items.title: Jetliner Road Shut Down After Driver Strikes Pedestrian Near Pearson Airport Monday Morning
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel police say a pedestrian was taken to hospital Monday morning after being struck by a vehicle at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. Police did not release details about the pedestrian beyond confirming the injuries were minor. Investigators also did not disclose what kind of vehicle was involved in the collision. Police closed westbound Jetliner Road at Airport Road following the crash and asked drivers to find alternate routes. Officers did not say how long the closure would last. Insauga notes Monday's crash was the second time in less than a week that a pedestrian has been struck by a vehicle on a busy Mississauga road.

items.title: Ontario's Solicitor General and Retail Council Leaders Join Peel Police's Two-Day Push Against Organized Retail Theft
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police are hosting a province-wide Retail Organized Crime Conference Tuesday and Wednesday at the Hyatt Place Toronto in Mississauga, bringing together law enforcement, retail industry leaders and public safety partners from across Ontario. Peel police said in a Monday news release that the two-day event aims to discuss emerging trends, investigative best practices and partnership-driven solutions to disrupt organized retail crime networks. Peel Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah, Deputy Chief Marc Andrews and Police Service Board vice-chair Omar Khan are set to welcome attendees including Ontario Solicitor General Michael Kerzner and the Retail Council of Canada's Rui Rodrigues. Insauga reports Peel police formed a specialized unit in September 2025 dedicated to tackling break-ins and large-scale theft of goods such as jewelry and clothing from retail businesses. Deputy Chief Andrews said at a July press conference at Square One Shopping Centre that the force's increased focus on a crime he described as having become endemic in the community has paid off so far.

items.title: Milev Wins J/24 North American Title at Port Credit Without Taking a Single Race
items.summary: Rossi Milev of Canada and his team aboard Clear Air won the 2026 J/24 North American Championship, hosted by Port Credit Yacht Club in Mississauga from September 30 to October 4. According to Sail-World, Milev relied on consistency rather than a single dominant finish to take the title, never winning a single race across the eight-race series against a 24-boat fleet from the United States and Canada. The regatta came down to the final day, with just three points separating the top five teams heading into Sunday's racing. Sail-World reports the fleet faced an onshore postponement that morning before launching at noon, when the breeze settled into the southwest and built to 15 knots with gusts to 20. Milev's Clear Air had sat as low as ninth place at one point before climbing back into contention, finishing with a scoreline of 3-2-2-10-4-2-2-4 and 19 net points after discarding a 10th-place result. Canada's Evan Petley-Jones finished second overall aboard Lifted with 21 points, two behind the champion, while also topping the Corinthian division among the 18 Corinthian teams in the fleet. Kurt Dammeier's Amuse Bouche rounded out the podium in third with 22 points, one point behind Lifted.
